tldr_label: TL;DR: US and Iran trade strikes as Iran hits Kuwait, Xi hosts Putin before Thursday's three-way summit, and Nvidia beats forecasts

tldr_bullets.label: Gulf
tldr_bullets.body: US jets struck an Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island. Iran answered with drones at Kuwait and Bahrain, and Qatar opened new talks with Tehran. [[TAG:danger:tit-for-tat]]

tldr_bullets.label: APEC
tldr_bullets.body: Xi met Putin in Shenzhen ahead of Thursday's first US-China-Russia leaders' meeting. In Manila, Trump announced a trade deal with the Philippines, though no terms have been released. [[TAG:info:Thursday]]

tldr_bullets.label: Nvidia
tldr_bullets.body: Nvidia beat forecasts in its first report without Jensen Huang and guided Q4 revenue to $126 billion to $134 billion. The shares rose modestly after hours following a weak day on Wall Street. [[TAG:success:beat and raise]]

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: The Knesset elected Yashar's Matan Kahana speaker by 66 votes to 52, giving Eisenkot's bloc control of the chamber's agenda. [[TAG:warning:Netanyahu weakened]]

tldr_bullets.label: Climate
tldr_bullets.body: A COP31 draft calling for faster fossil-fuel phase-out split negotiators. The EU warned it could make talks 'untenable.' [[TAG:warning:draft contested]]

sections.title: Gulf: Strike and Counterstrike
sections.summary: US hits Qeshm launch site; Iran fires at Kuwait and Bahrain; Qatar opens new talks

paragraphs.heading: Qeshm and Kuwait
paragraphs.body: CBS News and PBS reported that US jets struck an Iranian Revolutionary Guard missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Tuesday, hours after Iranian drones were launched at Bahrain. GMA and Dhaka Tribune reported that Iran then fired at Kuwait, with air defenses activated against drones aimed at Ali Al-Salem air base, which hosts US forces. It was the first attack on Kuwait since early September. Bahrain said it repelled Iranian attacks for the fourth time in six days. [[TAG:danger:widening strikes]]

paragraphs.heading: Shipping
paragraphs.body: Yahoo News reported that at least four tankers have been struck since Friday, and Gulf News reported a crew member missing after an ADNOC vessel was hit. The Revolutionary Guards say they are attacking tankers they deem to be transiting the strait illegally. The US maintains its naval blockade. [[TAG:danger:Hormuz contested]]

paragraphs.heading: Qatar Mediates
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported that Qatar warned the escalation poses a 'grave danger' and held new talks with Iranian officials to narrow the gap between proposals. Spokesperson Majed Al Ansari described the meeting as part of mediation efforts. Qatar called the attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain a dangerous escalation. [[TAG:info:talks continue]]

sections.sources: CBS News, PBS, GMA, Dhaka Tribune, Yahoo News, Gulf News, Euronews, Al Jazeera

sections.title: APEC: Leaders Converge
sections.summary: Xi meets Putin in Shenzhen before Thursday's trilateral; Trump touts Manila trade and Quad deals

paragraphs.heading: Shenzhen
paragraphs.body: The Standard, citing Xinhua, and China's government website reported that Putin arrived in Shenzhen early Wednesday for the APEC summit and met Xi the same day. CNBC set out what to watch at Thursday's three-way meeting with Trump, the first of its kind. [[TAG:info:trilateral Thursday]]

paragraphs.heading: Manila
paragraphs.body: Rappler and Anadolu reported that Trump announced what he called 'the biggest trade deal' with the Philippines, along with expanded defense cooperation. Marcos's office referred only to an 'understanding' on economic cooperation, there was no signing, and no terms have been released. Asia Media Centre reported that the Quad leaders announced critical-minerals agreements and an AI initiative. The ASEAN-US summit adopted principles against online scams. [[TAG:warning:no terms yet]]

sections.title: Nvidia Beats, Markets Wobble
sections.summary: Q3 tops forecasts and Q4 guide beats; Dow fell 1.6% before the report; Anthropic prices tonight

paragraphs.heading: Results
paragraphs.body: Reuters, via Investing.com, reported that Nvidia beat third-quarter forecasts and guided fourth-quarter revenue to $126 billion to $134 billion, above the roughly $125 billion analysts expected. The guidance assumes a lower gross margin and no China data-center sales. Constellation Research put quarterly revenue at $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. CoinDesk reported a $150 billion addition to the buyback authorization. Reports of the after-hours gain range from about 1% to nearly 4%. [[TAG:success:beat and raise]]

paragraphs.heading: Leadership
paragraphs.body: Euronext, carrying Reuters, reported that Nvidia's chairman said the company would not rehire Jensen Huang as CEO, and cited a Wall Street Journal report that the SEC is investigating the company. Reuters, via StreetInsider, said Nvidia would not take questions on the resignation. [[TAG:warning:SEC probe reported]]

paragraphs.heading: Markets
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post and Motley Fool reported that before the results the Dow fell 1.64%, the S&P 500 1.03% to its lowest close since July, and the Nasdaq 0.74%. FXStreet reported that Asian shares were mixed on Wednesday, with the Kospi leading gains. CNBC reported that Anthropic is likely to price its IPO above its $70 to $78 range, according to sources, ahead of trading on Thursday. [[TAG:info:Anthropic Thursday]]

sections.title: Israel: New Speaker
sections.summary: Knesset elects Yashar's Matan Kahana 66-52, ending Likud's hold on the chamber

paragraphs.heading: Vote
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel and CNN reported that the Knesset elected Yashar's Matan Kahana as speaker by 66 votes to 52, replacing Likud's Amir Ohana after a six-hour filibuster by Netanyahu allies. The Eisenkot bloc was joined by the Arab-majority Ra'am and Joint List parties. ABC News (Australia) reported that UTJ backed Likud's candidate, despite its informal talks with Eisenkot's bloc. Likud condemned the result. [[TAG:warning:Netanyahu weakened]]

paragraphs.heading: What It Unlocks
paragraphs.body: Reports said control of the speakership lets Eisenkot's allies advance bills to reverse parts of the judicial overhaul, impose prime ministerial term limits and set up an October 7 inquiry. Ynet reported that the bloc agreed to hold off on the overhaul repeal until Monday in exchange for an end to the filibuster. Netanyahu's caretaker government remains in office while coalition talks continue. [[TAG:info:agenda control]]

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Europe's negotiators join US-Ukraine talks for the first time; Russian An-12 crash kills 17

paragraphs.heading: Europe Joins
paragraphs.body: The Kyiv Post reported that Europe's full negotiating team, from France, Britain, Germany, Poland, Italy and the EU, joined online talks with Ukraine and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner for the first time, ahead of discussions in Berlin. The Kremlin has not formally confirmed European participation. Dawn reported that the sides discussed ways to draw Russia into talks. [[TAG:info:Berlin next]]

paragraphs.heading: Siberia Crash
paragraphs.body: The Kyiv Independent and US News, citing Izvestia, reported that a Russian military An-12 transport plane crashed in the Kemerovo region of Siberia, killing all 17 people aboard. Initial reports put the toll at three. The cause is under investigation, and Russia's defense ministry had not commented. [[TAG:danger:17 dead]]

sections.title: Climate and Chagos
sections.summary: COP31 draft urging faster fossil-fuel exit splits talks; Mauritius sets Chagos deadline

paragraphs.heading: COP31 Draft
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and Yahoo News reported that co-host Australia's draft cover decision urges countries to 'accelerate action for the phase out of fossil fuels' and calls for at least $120 billion in adaptation support. EU envoy Wopke Hoekstra warned that the draft as written could make talks 'untenable,' and major fossil-fuel producers oppose the phase-out language. Negotiations chief Chris Bowen said at least one more draft may come before the week ends. [[TAG:warning:deep divisions]]

paragraphs.heading: Chagos
paragraphs.body: Brit Brief and Mauritius News reported that Mauritius has set a December 2026 deadline for progress on the stalled Chagos Islands handover and warned of legal action against the UK. The deal has been in limbo since President Trump criticized it. Reports differ on whether the deadline is for ratification or for a roadmap. [[TAG:info:December deadline]]
